# Manual authoring implementation

Baseline: [project kickoff charter](../../TavernForge_Project_Kickoff.html). Scope: [manual authoring plan](../planning/MANUAL_AUTHORING.md) and [approved hybrid design](../DESIGN_DECISION.md). Implemented in the isolated next-increment checkout; integration commands and executed results belong in [current status](../STATUS.md). This report is not a release-readiness or device-verification claim.

## Implemented behavior

The library offers **Create manually** with an explicit choice among character V1/V2/V3, V2 CharacterBook, standalone V3 lorebook, and native World Info. A creation preview describes the exact format and default content. Only **Create draft** saves the selected template. Creation calls the same repository source-storage path as import, preserving the initial template as original and later authored revisions as current content. The local filename/title is separate from the JSON's name. Repeated creation taps are blocked while the operation runs. The screen's small title/selection state survives activity recreation.

`ManualAuthoring.kt` adds pure-format `createTemplate` and `planLoreEdit` extensions without changing the engine's core parser/validator/patch/export implementation. All templates parse, validate and identify as the selected format before success. V3 starts with the required empty group-only greetings array; standalone lorebook V3 does not receive an invented version marker. Optional artwork/timestamps/character books remain absent. Defaults are never applied when opening imported data.

Basic/Advanced modes expose format-specific named fields; a selected lore entry gets its own controls. Required labels are separate from creative completeness, and empty required strings remain valid. Optional values support explicit absence/removal; supported native nullable overrides offer **Inherit (null)** independently from false. Exact-value JSON input remains available for malformed/wrong-type/unknown content. String arrays have one input per exact string, including empty strings, commas and embedded newlines, with bounded paging and an exact-JSON alternative. Numeric text does not normalize an imported lexeme on open. Enum choices use pinned native numbers or book strings.

Writing guidance offers appearance, clothing, visual description, speech style, vocabulary and mannerism headings with an explicit description/personality destination. The resulting text opens as unapplied field input for review and writing. No additional top-level properties or hidden metadata are created.

## Lore commands and preservation

`LoreCommand` supports explicit embedded-book creation, add, duplicate, delete and complete entry-list reorder. `EntryLocator.ArrayIndex` and `NativeKey` remain session locators; they are not exported identifiers. Every command plans an atomic existing-engine patch and returns structured failure without partial application. Container type and membership checks precede mutation. New arrays use required V2/V3 fields, with insertion order 100 documented as an application default. Native entry values follow the pinned upstream template; original sparse entries are never backfilled.

Array duplication copies every entry value, changing only a present supported ID to an unused value; absent IDs stay absent. Native duplication copies all source values, changes the UID, and assigns display placement to the new entry. Existing object keys/UIDs are never renumbered. Numeric ID allocation considers equivalent numeric representations and bounds parsing/allocation. Unknown nested fields, nulls, number lexemes, extensions and native originalData remain in the preserved tree.

Array reorder changes only array order, retaining each entry's insertion order, priority and ID. Native reorder updates displayIndex, retaining runtime order, IDs, keys and all other values. Native add appends, and duplicate or AddEntry(after) inserts after the selected entry by assigning only the new entry's displayIndex. If adjacent indices tie or use extreme precision/scale, insertion fails with an explicit reorder-first message instead of silently rewriting existing values or expanding an enormous number. The explicit reorder operation can normalize display indices to consecutive integers. UI labels disclose display-order semantics and provide Move up/Move down actions without requiring drag. Entry selection is cleared after structural operations where its old index could identify a different entry.

Delete has a named confirmation. The original imported/created source stays intact. An invalid ID must be repaired before an identity-changing duplication; raw edit and deletion remain available. Input, byte, entry, depth, patch-count and cumulative patch-work limits remain active.

## Undo/redo and saving

`EditHistory` stores applied command batches against one immutable saved base. Undo/Redo replays active batches through the same engine; it does not reconstruct deleted data with inverse DTO serialization. New work after undo discards the redo branch. A grouped structural action is one history step.

The limits are 100 commands and 16 MiB encoded patch payloads, plus the existing 1000-patch and 64 MiB work/document limits. Exceeding a limit rejects the new command and preserves the input/history; it never drops a pending command required by save. Open field input blocks structural/history commands until explicitly applied or discarded. Undo back to the base produces an empty pending sequence and does not create a saved revision.

Save uses the existing expected persisted revision and immutable-original/current-snapshot repository contract. A conflict keeps pending history and input. A successful save closes the session and clears its history. Undo is explicitly **unsaved changes**, not durable revision recovery. ViewModel state survives activity recreation; process-death recovery restores only the last saved content and remains disclosed. Strict export continues through the revision-bound validation preview and Android CreateDocument flow.

## Verification handoff

The owner added 20 focused tests: ten pure-format cases, four history cases and six ViewModel cases. They cover all six template create/edit/export/reparse paths, original bytes and unknown values, array/native identity and reorder semantics, sparse imported entries, insertion placement, invalid/oversized commands, exact delete undo, redo branches, history/work limits, repeated creation, exact string-array values, absent/null/false distinctions, selection reset, guidance acceptance and conflict retention. Tests use synthetic in-code data; no credentials or private user content are fixtures.

Owner checks: `git diff --check` passes and app manifest/string XML parses. The supervisor's first compile reached the app and found an added storage error enum branch; that branch is now implemented. **No Gradle or device commands were run by this owner.** The supervisor must record final JVM/lint/build results and exercise creation, advanced controls, lore commands, undo/redo, restart/reopen and actual export on an authorized device/AVD before those paths are marked verified.

PNG/artwork, associations and Gemini have separately owned contracts and are staged for UI integration after this checkpoint. Source preservation and a passing schema report alone do not establish pinned SillyTavern runtime interoperability or complete charter acceptance.

## Subsequent UI checkpoints

The supervisor's manual checkpoint passed 244 JVM tests and app/data lint tasks. The next PNG/composition checkpoint passed 278 JVM tests, including five new app tests for explicit artwork saving, conflicting PNG candidates, picker cancellation, frozen/repeated output handling and stale/partial-write errors. These results were reported by the supervisor; this owner did not run Gradle or device commands.

`CompositionViewModel` and its screen now expose independent PNG/artwork intake, candidate review, saved character associations, linked lorebooks, same-schema embedding review, and PNG export review. Export writes only immutable validated plan bytes after the exact metadata replacements are accepted. A system-picker cancellation writes nothing. Closing a changed composition refreshes the inspector. JPEG original/derived conversion UI is the next staged integration over the separately implemented repository contract.

`GenerationViewModel` and its screen implement encrypted-key management, off-by-default text/image/follow-up grants, model metadata requests, fresh capability records, explicit request previews, generated draft review, and explicit acceptance through the same project repository. A model-list refresh replaces prior model instances; later pages replace duplicate names. Every actual provider call needs its own approval. Metadata listing, token counting and generation remain separate calls; there are no automatic retries. Permission flags currently last for this app process and restart off. The follow-up grant does not cause an automatic chain to run.

Key entry uses an ephemeral native password field with autofill, saved view state and personalized IME learning disabled. The Gemini window is secure against screenshots/recents capture. Plaintext input is not stored in ViewModel state, a Bundle, the recovery journal, logs or request bodies. Mutable key buffers are cleared after storage. Official Google AI Studio, pricing and rate-limit links open only through a user action. The local key-storage check itself makes no provider request.

Request previews show provider, endpoint, purpose, model, target, exact paged request body, one-call count, and output/response limits. Whole-project context is independently opt-in and disclosed as including unknown JSON values. Supported models receive structured-output schemas for new JSON, lore entries and typed greeting arrays; the independent format engine still validates output. Alternate/group greetings remain exact string arrays, with no delimiter conversion. Field acceptance shows the complete previous/proposed JSON values in paged views. Generated entries disclose removed generated IDs and fresh native identity/display placement. Unknown/version-mismatched responses cannot silently convert the project.

Only returned usage is shown; missing counts/cost stay unknown. Generated images are unaccepted memory objects until saved explicitly as original artwork, and attachment is another explicit action. Text acceptance rejects a stale target revision. Schema-invalid supported drafts may be accepted as local drafts while strict export stays blocked. No provider credentials or actual requests were used for owner verification; the new app tests use synthetic in-process responses. Initial Gemini tests required a scheduler fix because the service executes on its own Default dispatcher; the test now awaits completion before resetting Main. The final rerun is pending in supervisor evidence.
